meta.name: NURA Evidence Index
meta.purpose: Machine-readable index of every clinical claim in the NURA Biomarker Compendium: marker, claim, evidence grade, corroborating sources, and corroboration status. Retrieval layer for the product's insight engine, team reference, and NotebookLM source pack. No claim ships in-product on a single source.

grades.A: clinical guideline or meta-analysis of trials

meta.corroboration_rule: MULTI = independently supported by >=2 source types (guideline, meta-analysis, cohort). SINGLE = currently one strong source; must gain a second before the claim is used in-product.
meta.safety: All claims are educational information for consultation preparation. NURA never diagnoses, prescribes, or advises treatment changes.

claims.claim: Independently predicts all-cause mortality after MI (~HR 1.8 per SD); comparable discrimination to GRACE score post-MI
Stable-phase serial values predict long-term outcome better than acute-phase values; rising post-discharge trend is the alarm signal
Defining marker of myocardial injury (universal MI definition); re-rise after post-event decline signals new injury
claims.corroboration: SINGLE — textbook/guideline consensus; attach ESC Fourth Universal Definition citation before product use

claims.claim: Post-ACS very-high-risk target <55 mg/dL and >=50% reduction; <=40 mg/dL if recurrent event within 2 years
Secondary-prevention patients routinely miss LDL targets (therapeutic inertia documented in registries)
Secondary target after LDL goal met; catches residual particle risk in diabetes/high-TG/low-LDL states
Measure at least once in a lifetime; >50 mg/dL marks added heritable ASCVD risk (family screening relevant)
On statin therapy, hs-CRP predicts CV death and all-cause death more strongly than residual LDL-C (top quartile CV-mortality HR ~2.7)
~38% of statin-treated patients retain residual inflammatory risk (hs-CRP >=2 mg/L); MACE HR ~1.8
Mortality HR vs eGFR 95: ~1.03 at 60, ~1.38 at 45, ~3.11 at 15 (27M-participant consortium); multiplicative with albuminuria
Contrast-induced nephropathy: creatinine rise >=0.5 mg/dL or >=25% within 48-72h post contrast; ~7% incidence post-PCI; check creatinine 48-72h after procedure
Log-linear mortality association with no safe threshold: HR ~1.08/1.38/2.16 at uACR 10/30/300 vs 5 mg/g
U-shaped mortality; RAAS blockers raise K, diuretics lower it; monitoring within 1 week of start/up-titration, monthly x3, then quarterly year one
Statin practice: baseline ALT, recheck 4-12 weeks after initiation/dose change, then annually; action threshold >3x ULN; serious injury rare
Dose-response CV mortality association even within normal range: highest-vs-lowest HR ~1.59; ~+10% risk per 10 U/L
Albumin <3.5 g/dL: markedly higher mortality in stable CHD (10.2% vs 0.5%) and heart failure (adj. HR ~2.2); PhenoAge input
U-shaped mortality post-MI in diabetics; optimal band ~5.5-6.5%; OR ~1.89 below 5.5%, ~1.30 at >=8%; rapid swings carry independent risk
Anemia independently predicts mortality in elderly CVD (~2x in cohorts); on DAPT a falling Hb trend is a specific bleeding-watch signal
Four routine CBC indices are PhenoAge mortality-model inputs; RDW independently prognostic in cardiac patients
Standard 10/5 mmHg reduction cuts MACE ~28% in secondary prevention; intensive <120 SBP lowers mortality/MACE at cost of adverse events
RHR >80 bpm: RR ~1.45 all-cause mortality (1.2M-person meta-analysis); modifiable secondary-prevention target
Rapid gain ~2 kg over 3 days is the standard heart-failure fluid-retention early warning
claims.corroboration: SINGLE — standard ESC HF guideline self-care advice; attach guideline citation before product use

claims.claim: 9 routine biomarkers + age predict mortality/morbidity better than disease count (NHANES-derived, externally validated; applied in coronary disease)
Exercise-based cardiac rehab: CV mortality RR 0.74 (NNT 37), readmissions RR 0.82 (Cochrane, 85 RCTs / 23K patients)
Quitting after MI cuts mortality ~46% (OR 0.54, NNT ~13; meta-analysis of 12 cohorts, 5,000+ patients); recurrent MI and death reduced 30-50% across literature
+1,000 steps/day ~ -15% all-cause mortality; benefit plateau ~6,000-8,000/day for 60+ (8-10K younger); gains start well below 10K
Secondary prevention: CORDIOPREV RCT ~27% MACE reduction vs low-fat; Lyon 50-70% (older/smaller); Cochrane grades mortality evidence low-quality — promising pattern, uncertain effect size
